# Syrus plugin specification

Paste this file as a complete host contract when asking an LLM to write a Syrus plugin.

## Manifest schema

- `always` — Cleanup/lifecycle effect block retained after a once-enabled plugin is disabled.
- `author` — Author name used by the plugin inventory.
- `category` — Functional category from Syrus::Plugin::Category.
- `cli_commands` — Non-interactive server-backed CLI command declarations.
- `config_schema` — Operator-editable configuration field declarations.
- `conflicts_with` — Plugin manifest names that cannot be enabled together.
- `credential_type_names` — Shorthand list of credential type names without display metadata.
- `credential_types` — Credential type declarations with stable names and optional safe display text.
- `default_enabled` — Whether a newly discovered plugin starts enabled.
- `depends_on` — Required plugin manifest names.
- `description` — Short human-readable summary.
- `description_i18n_key` — Rails I18n key used instead of a literal summary.
- `disableable` — Whether an operator may disable the plugin.
- `display_name` — Human-readable plugin name.
- `display_name_i18n_key` — Rails I18n key used instead of a literal display name.
- `events` — Map of plugin event names to event declarations.
- `experimental` — Whether the plugin is gated as an experimental capability.
- `frontend` — Frontend assets relative to the plugin root: bundle, optional css, and i18n locale globs.
- `home_queue` — Default Solid Queue queue for plugin-owned work.
- `homepage` — Plugin documentation or project URL.
- `hosts` — Extension points this plugin makes available for other plugins.
- `icon_url` — Plugin icon URL or packaged icon path.
- `link` — Repeatable operator-facing link with label, URL, description, kind, and enabled-only behavior.
- `links` — Array form of link declarations.
- `long_description` — Longer operator-facing explanation.
- `long_description_i18n_key` — Rails I18n key used instead of a literal long description.
- `metrics` — Block declaring plugin-owned counters, histograms, gauges, and samplers.
- `name` — Stable plugin identifier passed to syrus_plugin; use lowercase snake_case.
- `on_boot` — Re-entrant process-level boot hook for work that is not a scoped registration.
- `optionally_depends_on` — Optional plugin manifest names used when present.
- `prepare_priority` — Ordering priority for prepare contributions.
- `provides` — Map of extension-point names to provider class-name strings (or arrays of them).
- `requires_syrus` — External gemspec metadata containing a Ruby Gem::Requirement for compatible Syrus releases.
- `route` — Repeatable HTTP route declaration: verb, path, and controller target.
- `suggests_enabling` — Evidence block and reason used to recommend an installed disabled plugin.
- `tick_interval` — Optional interval for lifecycle tick callbacks.
- `version` — Plugin version. Bundled plugins may use the host default; external plugins should match their gem version.
- `while_enabled` — Lifecycle effect block installed only while the plugin is enabled and healthy.

`frontend` accepts `bundle`, `css`, and `i18n`; locale globs must resolve under `app/frontend/i18n/locales/{en,de,la}/`. `cli_commands` entries require `path`, `summary`, and `handler`, and may declare typed `arguments` and `flags`.

## Extension points

- `adjudicator` — Marker interface for a rung-0 adjudicator (workflow-engine-v3). See [`Syrus::Plugin::Adjudicator`](../../../../lib/syrus/plugin/adjudicator.rb) for the interface contract.
- `admin_page` — Marker interface for plugin-provided admin pages. See [`Syrus::Plugin::AdminPage`](../../../../lib/syrus/plugin/admin_page.rb) for the interface contract.
- `affected_test_analyzer` — Interface for `:affected_test_analyzer` extension points. See [`Syrus::Plugin::AffectedTestAnalyzer`](../../../../lib/syrus/plugin/affected_test_analyzer.rb) for the interface contract.
- `agent_provider` — Interface module for agent provider implementations. See [`Syrus::Plugin::AgentProvider`](../../../../lib/syrus/plugin/agent_provider.rb) for the interface contract.
- `approval_provider` — Contract for optional plugins that may decide an already-pending exact invocation on behalf of a user. See [`Syrus::Plugin::ApprovalProvider`](../../../../lib/syrus/plugin/approval_provider.rb) for the interface contract.
- `artifact_renderer` — Interface for artifact renderer plugins. See [`Syrus::Plugin::ArtifactRenderer`](../../../../lib/syrus/plugin/artifact_renderer.rb) for the interface contract.
- `autofix_command` — Interface for `:autofix_command` extension points. See [`Syrus::Plugin::AutofixCommand`](../../../../lib/syrus/plugin/autofix_command.rb) for the interface contract.
- `build_system_graph_provider` — Interface for `:build_system_graph_provider` extension points. See [`Syrus::Plugin::BuildSystemGraphProvider`](../../../../lib/syrus/plugin/build_system_graph_provider.rb) for the interface contract.
- `callbacks` — Marker module for plugins that participate in the lifecycle callback system. See [`Syrus::Plugin::Callbacks`](../../../../lib/syrus/plugin/callbacks.rb) for the interface contract.
- `chat_identity_provider` — Owns a plugin-defined participant or agent identity on generic chat surfaces. See [`Syrus::Plugin::ChatIdentityProvider`](../../../../lib/syrus/plugin/chat_identity_provider.rb) for the interface contract.
- `chat_job_status_extension` — Adds plugin-owned actions to the chat Jobs workspace without teaching core which optional feature owns them. See [`Syrus::Plugin::ChatJobStatusExtension`](../../../../lib/syrus/plugin/chat_job_status_extension.rb) for the interface contract.
- `chat_mcp_tool_set` — Interface module for chat MCP tool set implementations. See [`Syrus::Plugin::ChatMcpToolSet`](../../../../lib/syrus/plugin/chat_mcp_tool_set.rb) for the interface contract.
- `chat_media_source` — Marker interface for a kind of media a chat can attach to a Job proposal or to feedback on an existing Job. See [`Syrus::Plugin::ChatMediaSource`](../../../../lib/syrus/plugin/chat_media_source.rb) for the interface contract.
- `chat_payload_contributor` — Marker interface for a plugin that adds its own data to the chat payload. See [`Syrus::Plugin::ChatPayloadContributor`](../../../../lib/syrus/plugin/chat_payload_contributor.rb) for the interface contract.
- `chat_prompt_injector` — Marker interface for a plugin that adds a section to the chat agent's system prompt. See [`Syrus::Plugin::ChatPromptInjector`](../../../../lib/syrus/plugin/chat_prompt_injector.rb) for the interface contract.
- `chat_provider` — Interface module for interactive chat provider implementations. See [`Syrus::Plugin::ChatProvider`](../../../../lib/syrus/plugin/chat_provider.rb) for the interface contract.
- `chat_turn_finalizer` — Marker interface for plugin-owned work that must run after an agent turn but before the chat releases its serialization lock. See [`Syrus::Plugin::ChatTurnFinalizer`](../../../../lib/syrus/plugin/chat_turn_finalizer.rb) for the interface contract.
- `chat_turn_lifecycle` — Allows an optional plugin to own the admission and execution context for a chat turn while core retains the generic invocation loop. See [`Syrus::Plugin::ChatTurnLifecycle`](../../../../lib/syrus/plugin/chat_turn_lifecycle.rb) for the interface contract.
- `chat_turn_orientation` — Marker interface for a plugin that takes over how one chat turn opens, based on the message that triggered it. See [`Syrus::Plugin::ChatTurnOrientation`](../../../../lib/syrus/plugin/chat_turn_orientation.rb) for the interface contract.
- `chat_workspace_lifecycle` — Lets an optional plugin provide a durable checkout around a chat turn. See [`Syrus::Plugin::ChatWorkspaceLifecycle`](../../../../lib/syrus/plugin/chat_workspace_lifecycle.rb) for the interface contract.

## Public host surface

The supported constants and members are reproduced below; the grouped human reference is [Plugin host API](host-api.md).

- `AgentInvocation::Result` (`public`, since 0.1.16) — Result value returned by plugin agent and chat provider invocations. Construction and the listed outcome, transcript, usage, process, and success readers are supported; invocation engine internals are not. Supported: class:`new`, instance:`aliveness_failed`, instance:`cache_creation_input_tokens`, instance:`cache_read_input_tokens`, instance:`cost_usd`, instance:`exit_status`, instance:`final_text`, instance:`input_tokens`, instance:`is_error`, instance:`operator_killed`, instance:`outcome`, instance:`output_tokens`, instance:`process_outcome`, instance:`session_id`, instance:`silent_timed_out`, instance:`spawned_process_id`, instance:`stopped`, instance:`success?`, instance:`timed_out`, instance:`transcript_jsonl`, instance:`transcript_path`, instance:`turns`.
- `Api::V1::Admin::BaseController` (`public`, since 0.1.16) — Base controller for plugin-owned administrative API routes. Subclasses may use inherited authentication, params, render, and policy helpers; filters and implementation details are not promised. Supported: instance:`params`, instance:`render`.
- `Api::V1::App::Admin::BaseController` (`public`, since 0.1.16) — Base controller for authenticated plugin routes in the app admin namespace. Only inherited request, rendering, and authorization behavior is supported. Supported: instance:`params`, instance:`render`.
- `Api::V1::App::BaseController` (`public`, since 0.1.16) — Base controller for authenticated plugin routes mounted in the application API. Only inherited request, rendering, and authorization behavior is supported. Supported: instance:`params`, instance:`render`.
- `ApplicationJob` (`public`, since 0.1.16) — Base class for plugin-owned Active Job classes and the host operational-log context hook. Core queue topology and execution callbacks are not public. Supported: class:`queue_as`, instance:`operational_log_context`.
- `ApplicationRecord` (`public`, since 0.1.16) — Active Record base for plugin-owned models using the Syrus primary database. Database internals and private core helpers are not promised. Supported: class:`belongs_to`, class:`has_many`.
- `ChatSession` (`public`, since 0.1.16) — Read access to a chat's identity, title, owner, repository, and messages. Turn orchestration, broadcasts, artifacts, and mutation helpers are not public. Supported: instance:`id`, instance:`messages`, instance:`repository`, instance:`title`, instance:`user`.
- `Current` (`public`, since 0.1.16) — Request-local access to the authenticated user and API user for plugin handlers. All other current attributes are internal and plugins must not assign these accessors. Supported: class:`api_user`, class:`user`.
- `Job` (`public`, since 0.1.16) — Read access to a work item's identity, state, title, repository, owner, and workflows, plus visibility-scoped queries. State transitions, callbacks, and unlisted persistence APIs are not public. Supported: class:`accessible_to`, class:`visible_to`, instance:`id`, instance:`repository`, instance:`state`, instance:`title`, instance:`user`, instance:`workflows`.
- `Mcp::Tools` (`public`, since 0.1.16) — Base module and response helpers for plugin MCP tools. Only the listed connection and response helpers are supported; core tool implementations are not. Supported: class:`invalid`, class:`success`, class:`with_database_connection`.
- `McpToolContext` (`public`, since 0.1.16) — Immutable authorization and request context passed to plugin tool handlers. Plugins may inspect the listed scope objects and predicates but must not construct or mutate contexts. Supported: instance:`chat?`, instance:`chat_session`, instance:`interactive`, instance:`job`, instance:`repository`, instance:`role`, instance:`run`, instance:`run?`, instance:`surface`, instance:`user`, instance:`workflow`.
- `OperationalLogging` (`public`, since 0.1.16) — Structured operational event sink for plugin diagnostics. Plugins may emit bounded events through ingest; subscriber installation and storage internals are not public. Supported: class:`ingest`.
- `PerformanceLogging` (`public`, since 0.1.16) — Performance instrumentation helper for timing plugin work through named phases. Event storage, thresholds, and request instrumentation are not public. Supported: class:`phase`.
- `ProcessRunner` (`public`, since 0.1.16) — Managed subprocess runner for plugin commands with host cancellation, timeout, confinement, and attribution. Plugins may use new, run, capture, start, mounts, and forwarded_env; backend and process-record internals are not public. Supported: class:`forwarded_env`, class:`mounts`, class:`new`, instance:`capture`, instance:`run`, instance:`start`.
- `Repository` (`public`, since 0.1.16) — Read access to repository identity, owner/name, archival state, and jobs, with active and user-scoped readable/writable queries. Credential fields, synchronization internals, callbacks, and unlisted mutations are not public. Supported: class:`accessible_to`, class:`active`, class:`writable_by`, instance:`archived_at`, instance:`id`, instance:`jobs`, instance:`name`, instance:`owner`.
- `Run` (`public`, since 0.1.16) — Read access to an execution attempt's identity, state, step, workflow, and job. Dispatch, lifecycle transitions, agent metadata mutation, and unlisted associations are not public. Supported: instance:`id`, instance:`job`, instance:`state`, instance:`step`, instance:`workflow`.
- `Syrus::Metrics` (`public`, since 0.1.16) — Non-blocking metrics facade for plugin-declared counters, gauges, and histograms. Plugins may fetch declared instruments; registry mutation and core metric declarations are not public. Supported: class:`counter`, class:`gauge`, class:`histogram`.
- `Syrus::Plugin::AdminPage` (`public`, since 0.1.16) — Marker contract for providers contributing administrative SPA pages through admin_pages metadata. Core navigation and route rendering internals are not public.
- `Syrus::Plugin::AgentProvider` (`public`, since 0.1.16) — Interface mixed into registered agent providers, including model catalog and configuration hooks documented by the module. Plugins may call syrus_plugin, syrus_plugin_definition, register!, enabled?, and default_version; Definition internals are not public. Supported: class:`default_version`, instance:`enabled?`, instance:`register!`, instance:`syrus_plugin`, instance:`syrus_plugin_definition`.
- `Syrus::PluginRegistry` (`public`, since 0.1.16) — Registry boundary for plugin manifests and extension-point providers. Plugins may register manifests and query providers for declared extension points; mutation, reset, health, and cache internals are not public. Supported: class:`extension_point?`, class:`providers_for`, class:`register`.
- `User` (`public`, since 0.1.16) — Read access to user identity, handle, display name, administrator status, repositories, and jobs. Credentials, preferences, callbacks, and unlisted persistence methods are not public. Supported: instance:`admin?`, instance:`display_name`, instance:`handle`, instance:`id`, instance:`jobs`, instance:`repositories`.
- `Workflow` (`public`, since 0.1.16) — Read access to a workflow attempt's identity, state, owning job, steps, and runs. Scheduling, transitions, repair behavior, and unlisted mutations are not public. Supported: instance:`id`, instance:`job`, instance:`runs`, instance:`state`, instance:`steps`.

## Packaging and testing

Plugins are trusted, in-process Rails Engine gems, not sandboxes. External gemspecs may depend only on Rails; use Ruby's standard library and the public host surface instead of third-party gems. Package prebuilt frontend assets and declare them with `frontend`. A plugin install or code change requires a Syrus restart.

Tests are required. Test each provider contract and plugin behavior, and include relocation/package coverage for external plugins. User-visible copy must be localized in English, German, and Latin.

## Mistakes to avoid

- Do not call unlisted core constants or members, or use `legacy` APIs from an external plugin.
- Do not put implementation classes in `provides`; register class-name strings that implement the linked interface.
- Do not add third-party Ruby gem dependencies or assume Syrus installs them.
- Do not run migrations when enabling a plugin; migrations run during deployment.
- Do not omit tests, the three locale bundles, `requires_syrus`, or the restart step.
